disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction is restructured to name automation that already exists in mature close processes while preserving a manual extraction lane as a first-class, resourced path for non-integrated or low-bandwidth environments, per the council's near-unanimous correction of tier-one-infrastructure assumptions. The step boundary is kept separate from matching (rejecting the maximalist merge, held against by six of seven members) because extraction/retranslation and matching are distinct computations with distinct failure modes requiring independently inspectable evidence. The risk-rated schedule and closing exchange rate inputs (ACR-R-01, ACR-R-07) remain explicit, and exchange differences are made separately visible per KB-08.

Matching survives (ACR-R-02) as its own step, restructured around a tiered automated/manual model. The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) rejected collapsing this into extraction; the seam between 'is the balance right' and 'do two balances agree' is kept inspectable. The manual matching lane is specified as permanently resourced, not a shrinking fallback, with a rehearsed degradation path, per emerging_economy's and pragmatist's converged non-negotiables, and intercompany identifiability is preserved per KB-14.

Investigation and classification survive essentially unchanged (ACR-R-03). The council was six-to-one against merging this with JE preparation: classification is the fork point between mechanical reclass and estimation treatment (KB-04, KB-10), and its rationale must remain independently inspectable from the resulting entry (KB-02). Agent assistance is confined to advisory retrieval and drafting; the human disposes on every item, not only a low-confidence tail, closing the threshold-ambiguity hitl_designer raised against generous automation of 'routine' items.

JE preparation is merged with preparer sign-off into one preparer-owned step, consistent with the full council's convergence that the same-actor handoff between preparing and signing off added no independent check. The merged step still consumes the prior-period error record (ACR-R-06) and preserves retrospective correction per KB-05; estimation-based entries retain a documented human basis per KB-04/KB-10.

Sign-off is merged into TS-04 rather than eliminated. The council rejected maximalist's elimination-with-no-successor-artifact position six-to-one: a named, timestamped preparer attestation must remain a distinct, affirmative output, not an inference drawn from system logging of draft submission. This satisfies the unconstrained_by_design flexibility on this step while preserving the evidentiary distinctness KB-02 requires.

Reviewer approval survives (ACR-R-09) and remains structurally separated from preparation by human identity, with agent assistance never substituting for or satisfying the separation (ACR-R-05), per the council-wide convergence on agent-non-actor status. It is merged with escalation into one controller-owned review event, following the five-member majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards-on-reconsideration) that the controller already holds the full context needed for both decisions in one sitting, while agentic_architect's timing concern is addressed by making the underlying ageing monitoring continuous rather than review-cadence-gated.

Escalation is merged into the controller's review step rather than fully absorbed into an unattended monitoring layer. The council majority held that detection of an aged item may be automated and continuous, but resolution of it is a judgment call (write off, pursue, accept explanation) requiring a named human decision of record — maximalist's 'recipient/resolver' framing was held against by five members. The design keeps alerting continuous (addressing the cutoff-discipline concern under KB-03/KB-05 that a monthly review pass would miss mid-cycle breaches) while requiring the controller's explicit, recorded escalation decision for every aged item.

Evidence retention and status reporting survive (ACR-R-08), restructured so that automated packaging and archiving are the mechanism but a named GL accountant affirmatively confirms completeness against the risk-rated schedule before status is reported, per the hitl_designer/finance_domain/pragmatist convergence against 'the system already logged everything' as a substitute for a human completeness check. Retention and reporting are specified to tolerate intermittent connectivity and avoid single-platform, per-seat dependency, per emerging_economy's non-negotiable, so the control functions identically across tier-one and constrained delivery environments.

steps.description: GL and comparison balances are extracted per the risk-rated schedule. Automated connectors handle integrated sources; a manual extraction lane (file upload, direct entry) is retained as a first-class, equally-governed path for non-integrated or low-connectivity sources, not a deprecated fallback. Foreign-currency balances are retranslated at the closing rate for every monetary item, with the resulting exchange differences captured as a separately visible output rather than netted into a generic balance. Missing feeds, stale rate tables, or out-of-tolerance retranslated balances are routed to the GL accountant as a named exception, never carried forward silently. Rate version, source system, and extraction mode (automated/manual) are logged on every run.
inputs: Reconciliation schedule by account risk rating
steps.name: Extract GL and comparison balances (automated and manual lanes)

steps.description: Transactions are matched between GL and comparison source using versioned, deterministic automated rules wherever data quality allows; everything the rules cannot resolve routes to a manual matching queue, which is resourced as a designed, permanent capability rather than a degraded exception path, and carries the same logging standard (preparer identity, timestamp, rationale) as the automated path. Every unmatched item is shown the rule(s) evaluated and why none fired. A defined, rehearsed fallback to full manual matching exists for engine outage or systemic mis-ruling, invoked and logged as an explicit event. Where in-scope accounts are intercompany, the matching configuration preserves full identifiability of intragroup positions for elimination.
steps.name: Tiered transaction matching

steps.description: Unmatched items are investigated, explained, supported with evidence and classified by the GL accountant, who remains the named, accountable decision-maker for every item. Agent assistance is limited to retrieving supporting documents, surfacing similar historical items, and drafting candidate explanations or classifications; the agent proposes, the human disposes (accept, reject, override with reason) on every item, including high-confidence ones. No item is auto-closed above a materiality or age threshold without a named human review. Classification is recorded as an artifact independent of any resulting journal entry, since it is what determines whether an item is a mechanical reclass or an estimation-based entry requiring documented judgment.
steps.name: Investigate and classify reconciling items

steps.description: Adjusting journal entries are prepared from explained reconciling items and the prior-period error record, with prior-period errors corrected retrospectively rather than folded into the current period. An agent may draft mechanical, rules-determinable entries as a first pass; the GL accountant edits and validates every draft and documents the judgment basis for any estimation-based entry (e.g. NRV write-downs, provisions). The former separate sign-off step is folded into this one, but its substance survives as a distinct, timestamped, named preparer attestation record certifying completeness and basis of the reconciliation and proposed entries — this is an affirmative act, not an inference drawn from draft submission or system logging. Agent involvement in drafting does not alter who is accountable for the attestation, nor does it create a second 'actor' for downstream separation-of-duties purposes.
steps.name: Prepare adjusting journal entries and preparer attestation

steps.description: An independent finance controller — a distinct human identity from the TS-04 preparer, a boundary enforced structurally and not satisfiable by agent involvement on either side — reviews and approves the reconciliation and its adjusting entries. An agent pre-screens for completeness, variance and anomaly, surfacing flags the controller resolves; the controller records a discrete approval decision for every item, with no batch or implicit approval for estimation-bearing or flagged items. Aging of reconciling items is monitored continuously by the system against the ageing threshold, with alerts surfaced to the controller as thresholds are crossed rather than withheld until the next scheduled review — a breach occurring mid-cycle must not wait for month-end to be seen. For every aged item, whether surfaced mid-cycle or at scheduled review, the controller records an explicit escalation decision (owner assigned, deadline, rationale), distinct from the approval decision though captured in the same sitting where timing allows.
steps.name: Reviewer approval and aged-item escalation

steps.description: Reconciliation evidence is packaged, timestamped and archived largely through automated capture, with amendments routed through a controlled, logged re-filing process rather than silent overwrite. Before status is reported upward, a named GL accountant (or delegate) affirmatively confirms evidence completeness against the risk-rated schedule — a checkpoint, not an inferred byproduct of system logging. Retention and reporting mechanisms are specified to function under intermittent connectivity and to produce exportable, platform-independent status output, so the control does not silently fail for teams without continuous connectivity or full platform licences.
steps.name: Retain evidence and report status
